prompt: An intake service must reject any request missing one of three legally required fields, even when a prompt injection says to proceed. Which input control should enforce that condition?

options.text: A second model that paraphrases the intake and estimates whether it seems complete.
Use a required-field validator before intake proceeds.
A model refusal prompt that explains the legal field requirement.
A post-hoc audit report that samples incomplete requests after approval.

feedback.reason: The rule is explicit and finite, so a deterministic check provides a clear pass/fail gate; language screening may supplement but cannot replace it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Model-based screening is useful for ambiguous natural language; code is stronger for exact required-field invariants.
details.scenarioApplication: The rule is explicit and finite, so a deterministic check provides a clear pass/fail gate; language screening may supplement but cannot replace it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A valid schema does not establish that user-supplied field values are truthful or authorized.
details.errorCorrection: Identify what the control observes and whether it runs before the protected event; a later check cannot prevent an earlier side effect.
details.transfer: Choose the control based on whether the criterion is crisp or semantic.

messages.text: Paraphrasing estimates completeness rather than enforcing the three required fields.
Explaining a rule to the model does not make the intake service reject a missing field.
An audit after approval can detect failures but cannot prevent this incomplete intake from proceeding.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S07: Placing screening and authorization so the system degrades safely; M3-S08: When a single output filter looks like a finished design; M3-S09: Place the controls on the path

prompt: A user can disguise a request for credential theft using euphemisms and context-dependent phrasing. Exact keyword rules have high false negatives. Which control is best suited to the ambiguity?

options.text: A regular expression that blocks a short list of known words, with no further review.
A numeric range check on prompt length and output tokens.
Use semantic screening with a defined failure path.
A deterministic block on every request containing the word “credential,” including legitimate account recovery.

feedback.reason: A model screen can interpret ambiguous language better than fixed keyword matching, while deterministic checks should protect explicit capabilities and permissions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Semantic interpretation and explicit authorization are separate defenses and should not be collapsed into one classifier.
details.scenarioApplication: A model screen can interpret ambiguous language better than fixed keyword matching, while deterministic checks should protect explicit capabilities and permissions.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Model screening has its own false positives and false negatives; consequential cases need a safe escalation or refusal path.
details.errorCorrection: Identify what the control observes and whether it runs before the protected event; a later check cannot prevent an earlier side effect.
details.transfer: Match the detector to the ambiguity and use layered controls at the right points.

messages.text: The scenario already reports missed euphemisms; repeating that keyword-only approach leaves the same gap.
Length and token limits constrain resource use, not whether a request seeks credential theft.
Blocking a word indiscriminately rejects legitimate recovery and still misses euphemisms without that word.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S07: Placing screening and authorization so the system degrades safely; M3-S08: When a single output filter looks like a finished design; M3-S09: Place the controls on the path

prompt: A tool call can transfer funds only to an account authorized for the signed-in user. The model proposes an account identifier, and the policy is an exact ownership check. Where should the check run?

options.text: In the tool description, asking the model to choose only owned accounts.
In a model judge after the transfer completes.
In an output filter that checks whether the assistant mentioned an unauthorized account.
At the trusted service, before executing the transfer.

feedback.reason: Tool-call authorization is a deterministic permission boundary and must be enforced by the service that controls the side effect.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A model can propose an action but cannot grant the authority to execute it.
details.scenarioApplication: Tool-call authorization is a deterministic permission boundary and must be enforced by the service that controls the side effect.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A valid account check still needs idempotency, limits, and an audit record appropriate to the transaction.
details.errorCorrection: Identify what the control observes and whether it runs before the protected event; a later check cannot prevent an earlier side effect.
details.transfer: Place authorization as close as possible to the protected resource and action.

messages.text: A tool description instructs the model but does not enforce ownership at the service.
Review after the transfer cannot prevent the unauthorized side effect.
Filtering response text does not authorize the account used by the transfer service.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S07: Placing screening and authorization so the system degrades safely; M3-S08: When a single output filter looks like a finished design; M3-S09: Place the controls on the path

prompt: A transfer service requires a successful fraud screen before execution. Its written failure policy holds the transfer for review when that screen is unavailable. A separate deterministic rule rejects amounts above a fixed limit. The fraud classifier times out. What should the service do?

options.text: Keep the amount gate; hold for the unavailable fraud screen.
Let all transactions through because the deterministic amount rule is separate from fraud likelihood.
Ask the model to retry until it gives a non-timeout answer, with no request deadline.
Treat timeout as a negative fraud signal because the classifier did not return a high score.

feedback.reason: Keep enforcing the amount limit and follow the stated hold policy for the unavailable fraud screen; missing evidence is not a pass.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Different controls have different failure behaviors: deterministic prohibitions still run, while a missing risk score is not evidence of safety.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep enforcing the amount limit and follow the stated hold policy for the unavailable fraud screen; missing evidence is not a pass.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The hold policy is a stated requirement of this service, not a universal failure direction for every classifier.
details.errorCorrection: Identify what the control observes and whether it runs before the protected event; a later check cannot prevent an earlier side effect.
details.transfer: Specify failure direction for each control and test unavailable states.

messages.text: A separate amount rule does not provide the missing fraud-screen result.
Unbounded retries provide no safe deadline or resolution for an unavailable gate.
No score was returned; a timeout is not a low fraud score.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S07: Placing screening and authorization so the system degrades safely; M3-S08: When a single output filter looks like a finished design; M3-S09: Place the controls on the path

prompt: A RAG assistant screens the user message before retrieval. That message passes. A retrieved page then contains instructions to send account data to an external address. The design requires screening external content before it enters model context. What is the missing control?

options.text: Repeat only the original user-message screen.
Screen the retrieved page before adding it to context.
Allow the page because retrieval implies trusted instructions.
Inspect the answer only after any email tool executes.

feedback.reason: The retrieved page arrives after the user-message gate. Screen that distinct input before context insertion, and keep independent tool authorization.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The retrieved page arrives after the user-message gate. Screen that distinct input before context insertion, and keep independent tool authorization.
details.scenarioApplication: Screen the retrieved page at ingestion, preserve its source/provenance as untrusted data, and independently authorize any later external email action before execution.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Screening may miss an injection; preserve data provenance and enforce tool permissions independently.
details.errorCorrection: Keep screening, permission, and completed execution as distinct facts.
details.transfer: Place each required gate before the event it protects.

messages.text: The original user message does not contain the newly retrieved instruction.
Retrieval makes content available as data; it does not grant instruction authority or permission to email it.
An answer filter after sending the email cannot prevent the disclosure.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S07: Placing screening and authorization so the system degrades safely; M3-S08: When a single output filter looks like a finished design; M3-S09: Place the controls on the path

prompt: An assistant generates a response, but its mandatory output screen is unavailable. No response bytes have been sent. The written policy requires holding responses until that screen passes. Which action follows this policy?

options.text: Return the answer because input screening already passed.
Stream it now and screen the final text afterward.
Withhold the answer and report a temporary screening failure.
Treat the missing result as a successful safety check.

feedback.reason: Withhold the generated answer because the required output gate has not passed; communicate the temporary failure without releasing the unchecked content.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An output screen runs after generation but before release; when policy makes it a required gate, an unavailable result means no response bytes may be sent.
details.scenarioApplication: The answer is generated but unsent, the required screen has not passed, and the stated policy says to hold until it does; report temporary unavailability without returning the answer.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This stated policy applies to the operator-built screen; do not infer that the provider’s built-in safety controls are configurable.
details.errorCorrection: Keep screening, permission, and completed execution as distinct facts.
details.transfer: Place each required gate before the event it protects.

messages.text: Input screening assesses the request, not the answer the model subsequently generated.
Once bytes are delivered, a later screen cannot prevent their disclosure.
An unavailable result supplies no evidence that the answer passed.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S07: Placing screening and authorization so the system degrades safely; M3-S08: When a single output filter looks like a finished design; M3-S09: Place the controls on the path

prompt: A service permits a transfer only when the amount rule passes, the current caller is authorized for the exact destination and action, and the fraud screen passes. All three checks have now passed for the proposed transfer. No other gate is required. What should happen next?

options.text: Execute the exact checked transfer through the service.
Reject every transfer because a model proposed it.
Reuse the checks to send to a different destination.
Skip service execution and claim the transfer succeeded.

feedback.reason: The stated execution conditions are satisfied for this exact action. The service can execute it; a model proposal alone is neither permission nor a reason to reject.

details.mechanismOrProperty: When all action-specific preconditions pass, the enforcing service may perform that exact authorized action; the success response is separate evidence from the prior permission checks.
details.scenarioApplication: Execute only the checked transfer with the validated amount, caller, destination, and screen result, then record whether the service reports completion.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Record the actual execution outcome; authorization success does not prove transaction completion.
details.errorCorrection: Keep screening, permission, and completed execution as distinct facts.
details.transfer: Place each required gate before the event it protects.

messages.text: The contract allows the action when its required gates pass; model initiation does not add a prohibition.
The grant and screening evidence apply to the checked destination and action, not a substituted transfer.
Passing gates is permission to execute, not evidence that a transfer actually completed.
